display.note: Each board is a slice of its pool's nodes, not a single physical GPU.

thermal.source: measured H100 thermal profiles (Phase 1), pooled across workloads, reading-weighted, forced monotone
thermal.disclaimer: Proxy from measured H100 data. Not measured on the simulated Alibaba hardware. The alert threshold and lag are assumptions; no measured reading reaches the threshold.

forecast.method: utilisation: persistence (current value held). temperature/power: thermal-proxy lag toward that load, at the current cooling state. A Kaplan-Meier survival projection of running jobs + queued/recent demand was also measured and is reported as projection_util_pct; it did not beat persistence at this horizon.

assumptions.note: submit time, duration, GPU request, priority and GPU model come from the Alibaba trace
the trace has no queue/start/eviction records; waits are reconstructed by simulation
a job's whole GPUs must sit on one node; fractional requests share one GPU
jobs run only on their recorded GPU model; no cross-hardware speedup data exists
worker_count ignored; gpu_request_recorded_count is the job's total request
HP jobs may evict running spot jobs; evicted work restarts from scratch (switchable to resume)
whole nodes of the observed shapes are added/removed so offered load ~ target (default 0.85); a load sweep is reported
a window starts with jobs submitted earlier and still running (assumed zero historic wait); ~5% of jobs hold ~95% of GPU-seconds
schedulers do not see true durations except the oracle baselines
no user runtime estimates exist; backfill uses oracle / noisy / pool-median estimates, reported separately

notes: Waits, starts, evictions and node placement are simulated, not observed.
Temperature and power are a proxy from measured H100 profiles, not Alibaba measurements.
Queue order is the policy's ordering key; rl_ppo picks among candidates so its list is arrival order.

scenario.name: node_failure
scenario.note: Board 8 (A10 pod) loses its nodes at hour 6 and recovers at hour 10
